summary: A website for sharing PDFs with viewers. Users can upload PDFs and share them with others who can view them online. Admin controls (kick/ban users) are being added for the site owner.
architectural_notes: PDF upload size workaround: split large PDFs into parts under 2MB and upload separately; IC ingress message limit is ~2MB
known_issues: Chunked upload feature build has failed multiple times; large PDFs (>2MB) cannot be uploaded in a single message on IC
PDF uploads failing even for small files (0.39 MB) — root cause unknown; full PDF integration redo requested
Upload fails with 'Unauthorized: Only users can start uploads' — backend auth check is rejecting the upload caller
PDFs don't open when clicking 'Open' on the public gallery page (Version 6)
Upload fails with 'Failed to start upload: Actor not available' — actor not initialized before upload attempt (Version 7)
Upload page 'Initializing connection…' message can hang indefinitely (reported hanging for 10+ minutes) — actor initialization does not timeout or retry automatically
Upload fails with 'Authorization failed. Please log out and log in again, then retry.' — backend is still rejecting authenticated users; access control too restrictive (Version 10)

existing_features.title: Build a PDF upload page for the site owner/admin: include a file picker restricted to .pdf files, a title input field, and an upload button. On successful upload, display the generated shareable link for that PDF.
Build an admin dashboard page that lists all uploaded PDFs showing title and upload date. Each entry should have a copy-link button and a delete button.

Build a public PDF viewer page accessible at /view/<shareId>. Fetch the PDF binary from the backend by share ID and render it inline using a PDF rendering library (e.g., react-pdf or an embedded <iframe> with a Blob URL). Show the PDF title at the top.

Apply a clean, modern visual theme with a dark navy and warm amber accent color palette, crisp sans-serif typography, card-based layouts with subtle shadows, and smooth hover transitions. Apply this style consistently across all pages.
Use a generated logo image (pdf-share-logo.dim_256x64.png) in the site header/navbar.

On the admin Dashboard page, add an inline edit control for each PDF entry's title. Each row should include an edit (pencil) icon button that opens an editable text field pre-filled with the current title and a save button. On save, call the backend rename function and refresh the list. Show a loading state during the save and display an error message if the update fails.

On the PDF viewer page (/view/<shareId>), add a 'Next PDF' button that navigates the user to the viewer page of the next uploaded PDF. 'Next' should be determined by upload order (ascending by upload timestamp). If the current PDF is the last one uploaded, the button should be hidden or disabled. Fetch the full list of PDF metadata from the backend to determine the next share ID.

Rewrite the frontend PDF upload flow in UploadPage.tsx to use the new chunked upload backend API. On file selection, split the PDF ArrayBuffer into chunks of 500 KB, call startUpload to initialize, then sequentially call uploadChunk for each chunk with retry logic (up to 3 retries per chunk on failure), then call finalizeUpload. Display a progress bar showing chunk upload progress (e.g., '3 of 7 chunks uploaded'). Show a clear error message with the specific failure reason if any step fails, and allow the user to retry the upload.

Rewrite the frontend PDF retrieval and rendering flow in ViewerPage.tsx to use the new chunked retrieval backend API. Fetch the chunk count via getPdfChunks(shareId), then sequentially fetch each chunk via getPdfChunk(shareId, chunkIndex), reassemble all chunks into a single Blob, create an object URL, and render the PDF in an iframe. Show a loading progress indicator while chunks are being fetched. Display a clear error message if retrieval fails.

Update the React Query hooks in useQueries.ts to expose the new chunked upload and chunked retrieval functions, replacing the old single-call upload and fetch hooks. Ensure the dashboard list, delete, and rename hooks continue to work with the updated backend API signatures.

Verify that the frontend actor in `useActor.ts` / `useQueries.ts` is constructed with the authenticated identity (not anonymous) when the user is logged in via Internet Identity before calling `startUpload`. If the actor is being created anonymously even when the user is authenticated, ensure it is rebuilt with the correct identity so the backend receives a non-anonymous principal.

Create a public gallery page at '/' or '/gallery' that lists all uploaded PDFs without requiring login. Each entry should display the PDF title and upload date, and clicking an entry should navigate to the existing viewer page at /view/<shareId>. This page must be accessible to any visitor without authentication.

Fix the 'Open' button on the public gallery page (GalleryPage.tsx) so that clicking it successfully navigates the user to the PDF viewer page at /view/<shareId>. Investigate why navigation fails (e.g., broken route linking, missing shareId in card data, incorrect href/navigate call) and ensure each gallery card's 'Open' button correctly routes to the viewer for that PDF.

Verify that the ViewerPage.tsx correctly handles the shareId route parameter and that the chunked PDF retrieval flow (getPdfChunks → getPdfChunk → reassemble → iframe render) completes successfully when navigated to from the gallery. If the viewer page fails to load the PDF after navigation, fix the root cause (e.g., incorrect param extraction, actor not ready, premature fetch before actor is initialized).

In UploadPage.tsx, guard the upload flow so it does not attempt to call startUpload until the actor is confirmed to be initialized and non-null. Before invoking any upload step, check that the actor reference returned from useActor (or the equivalent hook) is available; if it is not yet ready, show a loading/waiting state rather than immediately throwing 'Actor not available'. Only proceed with the chunked upload sequence once the actor is definitively available.

In useQueries.ts (and/or useActor.ts integration), ensure the actor used for upload mutations is always sourced reactively from the query cache or hook state so that if the actor initializes after the component mounts (e.g., because the Internet Identity identity loads asynchronously), the upload mutation automatically picks up the latest actor instance rather than capturing a stale null reference at component mount time.

Update the public gallery page (GalleryPage.tsx) so that it is the default home route ('/') and automatically reflects any newly uploaded PDF immediately after upload — ensuring the list query is invalidated/refetched after a successful upload so the new entry appears without requiring a manual page refresh.

Update the actor initialization logic in UploadPage.tsx so that when initialization is pending or fails, the app retries the connection targeting only active/available IC nodes rather than retrying blindly against all nodes. After 5 seconds of waiting, display a visible 'Retry connection' button that the user can click to manually trigger a fresh initialization attempt. Each retry should attempt to re-create the actor using the existing useActor hook mechanism. Clear the error/waiting state and resume normal initialization flow once the actor is successfully created.

In UploadPage.tsx, update the error messaging so that when an authorization error is returned from the backend, it clearly informs the user that upload is open to all logged-in users and prompts them to ensure they are logged in, rather than displaying confusing 'log out and log in again' instructions.

Add an Admin Users panel to the Dashboard page (DashboardPage.tsx) — visible only when the authenticated user is the admin — that lists all principals who have uploaded PDFs (derived from uploaded PDF metadata), with a 'Kick' button next to each uploader. Clicking 'Kick' calls the backend `kickUser` function for that principal and shows a confirmation before executing. Also display a 'Banned Users' section listing currently banned principals, each with an 'Unban' button that calls `unbanUser`. Show loading and error states for all kick/unban actions.

Add React Query mutation hooks in `useQueries.ts` for `kickUser(principal)`, `unbanUser(principal)`, and a query hook for `listBannedUsers()`. These hooks must use the authenticated actor instance (same pattern as existing mutation hooks) and invalidate the banned users query after a successful kick or unban.

Create a new page at '/feed' (or '/all') that displays all PDFs uploaded by all users/accounts in a single, publicly accessible feed. Each entry should show the PDF title, uploader's principal (truncated for readability), upload date, and an 'Open' button that navigates to the existing viewer at /view/<shareId>. The page must be accessible without authentication, using the existing anonymous-compatible listPdfs() backend call. Sort entries by upload timestamp descending (newest first).

Add a 'Feed' navigation link in the site header (Header.tsx) that routes to the new all-PDFs feed page. The link should follow the same active-route highlighting pattern used by the existing Gallery, Upload, and Dashboard nav links.

Register the new feed page route in App.tsx (TanStack Router) so that navigating to '/feed' renders the new FeedPage component. Ensure the route does not require authentication and does not conflict with existing routes.

new_feature_requests.summary: PDF upload functionality for the owner/admin
PDF viewer for shared documents accessible by viewers
Shareable link generation for uploaded PDFs

Create a backend data model and actor to store uploaded PDF metadata (title, file name, unique share ID, upload timestamp, and binary content) with functions to: upload a PDF, retrieve a PDF by share ID, list all uploaded PDFs, and delete a PDF by share ID.
Allow editing/changing the title of an uploaded PDF

Add a backend function to update the title of an existing PDF entry by its share ID. The function should accept a share ID and a new title string, update the stored metadata, and return a success or error result.
Add a 'Next PDF' button on the viewer page that automatically navigates to the next uploaded PDF when the current one finishes
Redo the PDF upload integration to fix upload failures (even for small files under 2MB)

Rewrite the backend PDF storage and upload logic in main.mo to use a reliable chunked upload approach: split incoming PDF binary data into small chunks (e.g., 500 KB each), store chunks separately in stable memory, and reassemble on retrieval. Expose backend functions: startUpload(title, shareId, totalChunks), uploadChunk(shareId, chunkIndex, chunkData), finalizeUpload(shareId), getPdfChunks(shareId) returning chunk count and metadata, getPdfChunk(shareId, chunkIndex) returning a single chunk blob, listPdfs(), deletePdf(shareId), and renamePdf(shareId, newTitle). Ensure all existing metadata fields (title, shareId, uploadTimestamp) are preserved.

Fix the backend `startUpload` function so that it correctly identifies authenticated callers. The current access control check is rejecting legitimate upload requests with 'Unauthorized: Only users can start uploads'. Inspect the caller identity check in the `startUpload` handler — ensure it accepts any non-anonymous principal (i.e., a real Internet Identity user) rather than applying an overly restrictive check such as comparing against a hardcoded admin principal or using a broken identity comparison. The fix must allow authenticated Internet Identity users to call `startUpload`, `uploadChunk`, and `finalizeUpload` successfully.
Create a universal/public page where all uploaded PDFs are visible to anyone who visits the website, without needing a specific share link
Ensure the backend listPdfs() function is callable by anonymous (unauthenticated) principals so the public gallery page can fetch the PDF list without requiring the caller to be logged in.

Improve actor initialization on the upload page: add a retry mechanism that attempts to reconnect only to active/available IC nodes, with a visible 'Retry connection' button that appears after a few seconds if initialization is still pending.

Allow any authenticated Internet Identity user (not just a specific admin) to upload PDFs. Remove or relax the access control check in the backend so that any logged-in user can call startUpload, uploadChunk, and finalizeUpload.

In the backend (main.mo), update the access control checks for startUpload, uploadChunk, and finalizeUpload so that any non-anonymous authenticated Internet Identity principal is permitted to call them. Remove any check that compares the caller against a hardcoded admin principal or a specific allowed list. The only restriction should be that the caller is not the anonymous principal.
Add admin commands to kick/remove users from the platform (admin-only controls for the site owner)

Add a backend `kickUser(principal: Principal): async Result` function to the main actor that allows the designated admin (the canister owner/controller) to ban a user principal from uploading. Store banned principals in a stable data structure. When a banned principal calls `startUpload`, `uploadChunk`, or `finalizeUpload`, reject them with a clear 'You have been banned from uploading' error. Also add `listBannedUsers(): async [Principal]` and `unbanUser(principal: Principal): async Result` functions, both restricted to the admin caller only.
Create a page that aggregates and displays all PDFs uploaded by all users/accounts in one place
